text:
sam: quick sync — ran a short bring-up for polaris-7b (v0) across fp16 / int8 / int6. attached the microbench numbers and a small slice eval. need a recommendation for routing + a short blurb for GTN.

mica: share the slice and the perf table?

sam: pasted below. slice = 2k conversational prompts, mixed short/long (avg 80 toks).
```
// perf summary (avg over 10 runs)
model | precision | p95 latency (token/ms) | tokens/sec | $/1M tokens
polaris-7b fp16 | fp16 | 12ms/token | 85 t/s | $6.8
polaris-7b int8  | int8 | 9ms/token  | 115 t/s | $4.9
polaris-7b int6  | int6 | 8.2ms/token| 125 t/s | $4.2
```
quality delta on our QA slice (relative to fp16) = BLEU-like metric / human pass rate on key intents:
- int8: -0.9% overall, no regressions on safety or slots
- int6: -2.7% overall, regressions concentrated in long-form summarization (~6% drop)

sam: my take — int6 gives great unit-econ but we see a concentrated longform regression. think hybrid routing + cache/cutoff for long summaries is the sweet spot.

rachel: agree. proposal: default route int6, route to int8 for requests flagged by length or hallucination-signal, and fallback to fp16 only for highest-importance enterprise customers. add an eval hook to monitor "summary-fidelity" metric and an hourly sampling of real traffic for human checks.

raj: what about cold-start ai latency? int6 seems slightly better, but p95 difference small. are there memory-instability risks with int6 KV cache growth?

mica: we saw occasional cache mismatch on int6 in earlier bring-ups — fixed by forcing consistent quantize/dequantize path in runtime. add a runtime flag `--quant-stable=true` for canary.

ops-bot: deploy canary created: canary/polaris7b-int6-2026-05-14 at commit abc123. 10% traffic, region us-west-2.

zoe: For GTN blurb, keep it simple: "Polaris 7B (int6) — ~38% token cost reduction vs fp16 with comparable conversational quality for short/medium responses. Use hybrid routing for long summaries to avoid fidelity loss." Want me to draft the short one-pager?

sam: yes please. also include an explicit routing rule and signal list. I'm thinking:
- route to int6 when prompt tokens + estimated response <= 256
- route to int8 when estimated response between 257-1024 or when `summary_request=true`
- route to fp16 only if `enterprise_sla=true` or if fallback from int8 fails quality guard

rachel: add monitoring signals:
- summary-fidelity (hourly) : human-pass-rate on sampled summaries
- perplexity-delta: drift detection vs baseline
- latency-p95 and error-rate by precision
- token-econ dashboard showing $/1M tokens by route

raj: ops ask: keep a quick rollback plan: if summary-fidelity drops >3% over 1h, auto-rollback int6 canary and scale int8 fallback to 30%.

mica: also add a small prompt-level heuristic for routing — if prompt contains "summarize" or >3 question marks or "TL;DR" tag, bias to int8.

sam: ok next steps action list:
- zoe: draft GTN one-pager + 2-line product blurb (eta EOD)
- mica: add `--quant-stable=true` flag and run internal regression (eta 24h)
- rachel: implement routing config + metrics in canary (eta 48h)
- raj / infra: validate KV stability on int6 under burst (eta 48h)
- ops-bot: keep canary at 10% and emit hourly snapshots

zoe: will do. drafting now. :memo:

sam: thanks all. will post final recommended routing after we get the runtime flag results.

mica: tiny note — capture example failing case for int6 and add to the eval set before rollout. helps avoid silent regressions.

sam: good call. attaching a gist with 6 failing examples in thread (will add separately).

zoe: ping @product for visibility? @product: FYI, prepping GTN copy for cost-savings messaging.

product: thanks, appreciated. can you include an estimated ARR impact if 40% of traffic is moved to int6?

zoe: will compute once we have traffic mix numbers.

sam: end-of-thread checkpoint: aim to have canary gating metrics green in 72h then prepare gradual ramp to 50% with automated rollback triggers.
